findings.title: Rejecting cookies requires paying or subscribing
findings.detail: The only reject option found was tied to a subscription or payment, so we did not click it.
findings.law: UK GDPR Art. 4(11) and 7(4) (consent must be freely given). ICO allows 'consent or pay' only if it's fair

findings.title: Paid alternative may undermine freely given cookie consent
findings.detail: The banner used a pay-or-consent model, and the audit could not successfully select a standalone rejection option. The Guardian's policy says non-essential cookies and personalised advertising are based on consent, raising a question whether consent obtained in this way is freely given.
findings.law: UK GDPR Art. 4(11) and Art. 7; PECR reg. 6
findings.policy_quote: Place non-essential cookies and similar technologies including for personalised advertising as set out in the “Privacy settings” link on our sites in the footer of every page, which you may withdraw at any time depending on whether you are able to read the Guardian ad free or have a Guardian Ad-Lite subscription.
findings.reasoning: Consent must be freely given and withdrawing it must be as easy as giving it; ICO guidance also requires rejecting to be as easy as accepting. This is medium rather than high because the evidence does not show what cookies or tracking occurred, and the fairness of the paid alternative may depend on factors such as price and the precise choices offered.

ai_review.summary: The evidence establishes a significant concern with the site's pay-or-consent mechanism and whether consent for non-essential cookies or personalised advertising is freely given. However, the audit does not provide network-request or cookie evidence showing that advertising, profiling, or other non-essential tracking actually started before a choice or continued after rejection. The assessment therefore records a medium-level consent and fairness concern rather than a higher-severity tracking finding.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: False. Method: pay_or_consent. Buttons clicked: Reject all and subscribe.
